newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Canadian charged with child sex in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Canadian charged with child sex in Cambodia.

text.p: A Cambodian court on Friday ordered a Canadian national to be held in custody for up to six months for further investigations after prosecutors charged him with child sex offences, officials said.

Manfred Horst Albert Gast, a 53-year-old Canadian of German origin, denied charges brought against him under a law against trafficking in women and children, Phnom Penh Municipal Court Deputy Director Nub Sophan told reporters.
Gast, the second foreigner charged under the new legislation in the past week, was arrested at a Phnom Penh hotel on Tuesday.

Cambodia Interpol chief General Skadavy M. Ly Roun said on Thursday that six boys aged under 15 had claimed they had sex with Gast. The general showed reporters dozens of graphic photographs of prepubescent boys, saying they were found in Gast's luggage.
The same court earlier this week ordered Frenchman Amedee Hennion, 54, remanded in custody for up to six months after prosecutors charged him with child sex offences.
The two men face up to 20 years in prison if convicted.
Child welfare groups, which have long warned that Cambodia has become a haven for local and foreign paedophiles, have welcomed the first arrests of suspected child molesters since 1995.
General Skadavy M. Ly Roun has pledged more arrests.
The crackdown is believed to have been ordered by co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen.
